balanceSheet.title: Shareholders' equity vs total equity incl. perpetuals & NCI
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity belongs to ordinary holders. Total equity incl. perpetuals & NCI adds the HK$7.9bn of perpetual capital securities (quasi-equity, ranks ahead of ordinary shareholders, ~HK$286m/yr distributions) and non-controlling interests -- both deducted once in the DCF's equity bridge.

For CK Asset Holdings Limited (長江實業集團有限公司): the gap between the two lines is exactly the stock the DCF subtracts before arriving at ordinary equity value; it has been a steady ~HK$11-12bn since the FY2021 perpetual securities were issued.

What to watch:

  • The gap widening (more perpetuals/NCI issued) without a matching rise in consolidated earnings
  • Equity dominated by IAS 40 investment-property and development-inventory carrying values, not retained operating earnings

investmentProperty.title: Investment property acquisitions
investmentProperty.content:
Cash spent adding to the investment-property portfolio (the ~10%-of-revenue rental segment: Cheung Kong Center II, Civitas and similar), separate from the fixed-asset CapEx already shown elsewhere.

For CK Asset Holdings Limited (長江實業集團有限公司): this line is lumpy by design -- HK$229m in FY2025 versus HK$2,893m in FY2024 and HK$12,950m in FY2018 -- because it tracks discrete acquisitions, not steady maintenance capex. The DCF folds a smoothed version into its capex_pct assumption rather than projecting single years.

What to watch:

  • A large spike signalling a specific acquisition (check the filing for the asset)
  • Multi-year troughs, which just mean no acquisition that period, not capital starvation

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For CK Asset Holdings Limited (長江實業集團有限公司): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For CK Asset Holdings Limited (長江實業集團有限公司): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts interest income (SBC is a disclosed zero -- no share option scheme) -- the cash the consolidated operating business could actually distribute.

For CK Asset Holdings Limited (長江實業集團有限公司): this is only the consolidated operating business (Greene King pubs ~45% of revenue, property sales ~35%, rental ~10%, hotels ~8%). It excludes JV dividends/loan repayments (HK$3,310m FY2025) from the infrastructure JVs, Hui Xian, Fortune and Prosperity stakes, which never hit consolidated OCF -- the DCF adds those separately at book value in the equity bridge (~HK$72bn, HK$20/share) rather than valuing them off this series.

What to watch:

  • Development-inventory releases swinging OCF by tens of billions in a single year (FY2022 owner FCF was HK$942m, FY2025 was HK$14.3bn) -- never read one year as the run rate
  • Greene King's contribution margin (~7% EBITDA margin after its restructuring) dragging on consolidated FCF despite being the largest revenue segment

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For CK Asset Holdings Limited (長江實業集團有限公司): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For CK Asset Holdings Limited (長江實業集團有限公司): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For CK Asset Holdings Limited (長江實業集團有限公司): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is consolidated turnover across the four reporting segments: Greene King pubs (~45%, the single largest segment), property sales (~35%, lumpy by completion schedule), property rental (~10%) and hotels (~8%). It excludes the equity-accounted infrastructure JVs, Hui Xian REIT and the Fortune/Prosperity REIT stakes entirely -- those sit in the DCF's equity bridge, not here.

For CK Asset Holdings Limited (長江實業集團有限公司): property-sales recognition timing (Blue Coast handovers, the FY2027 gap before Victoria Blossom and Borrett Road Ph2) drives most of the swing in this line, not underlying demand -- read the DCF's growth_rationale before reacting to one year's number.

What to watch:

  • Property-sales recognition gaps vs genuine demand softness
  • Pub revenue resilience (or further Greene King impairments) given its 45% weight
  • Interim rows show seasonality and the handover schedule

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For CK Asset Holdings Limited (長江實業集團有限公司): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
